what_its_for: Rasburicase is used to treat or prevent a condition called tumor lysis syndrome (TLS), which happens when cancer cells break down quickly during chemotherapy and release harmful substances into your blood. This drug helps lower high levels of uric acid in your blood, which can damage your kidneys if left untreated.
how_to_take: Rasburicase is given to you as an IV infusion (a slow injection into your vein) by a nurse or doctor in a hospital or clinic setting. You will NOT give yourself this medication at home. Each infusion is given over about 30 minutes. Do not shake the IV bag or tubing during the infusion. Tell your nurse right away if you feel any discomfort, itching, swelling, or trouble breathing during the infusion.
dosing: Your doctor will calculate your dose based on your body weight (usually 0.2 mg per kilogram). You will typically receive one dose once a day for up to 5 days. Your dosing schedule will be set by your cancer care team and is closely monitored. Never try to adjust your own dose.
missed_dose: Because this medication is given by healthcare professionals in a clinical setting, missed doses are managed by your medical team. If you are unable to keep a scheduled appointment, contact your doctor or clinic as soon as possible so they can reschedule your treatment. Do not try to make up a missed dose on your own.
storage: You will not store this medication at home. The hospital or clinic handles all storage. For your information: the unmixed powder must be kept refrigerated between 36°F and 46°F (2°C to 8°C) and must not be frozen. Once mixed, the solution should be used within 24 hours and kept refrigerated.
what_to_avoid: Do not take any medications that contain glucose-6-phosphate dehydrogenase (G6PD) without telling your doctor first. Avoid this drug entirely if you have a G6PD deficiency, as it can cause a dangerous breakdown of red blood cells. Do not breastfeed while receiving this medication. Avoid getting pregnant during treatment. Tell your doctor about ALL medications, vitamins, and supplements you take before starting rasburicase.
when_to_call_doctor: Call your doctor or go to the emergency room immediately if you experience: trouble breathing or wheezing, chest pain or tightness, severe allergic reaction (swelling of face, lips, tongue, or throat, hives, dizziness), unusual back or side pain, blood in your urine, signs of anemia such as extreme tiredness or pale skin, yellowing of your skin or eyes (jaundice), fever or chills, or if you feel very unwell at any point during or after treatment.
when_it_works: Rasburicase works very quickly. It begins lowering uric acid levels in your blood within a few hours of the first dose. Your medical team will monitor your blood levels throughout your treatment to make sure the medication is working properly.
special_populations: PREGNANCY: This drug may harm an unborn baby. Use effective birth control during treatment and tell your doctor immediately if you become pregnant. BREASTFEEDING: Do not breastfeed while receiving this medication, as it may pass into breast milk and harm your baby. G6PD DEFICIENCY: This drug must NOT be used if you have G6PD deficiency, as it can cause a life-threatening condition called hemolytic anemia. All patients should be tested for G6PD deficiency before starting treatment. CHILDREN: This medication is approved for use in children and the dose is based on body weight. KIDNEY OR LIVER PROBLEMS: Tell your doctor if you have kidney or liver disease, as this may affect your treatment plan.
